title: Bezalel's hands (Exodus 35:30–35)
hookLine: the first person filled with the Spirit in the Bible is a craftsman

lines: NOT A PROPHET. NOT A PRIEST.
cards: Quick question. In the Bible, who is the first person God is said to fill with his spirit? A prophet, you'd guess.
A priest. Moses, maybe. Pharaoh once said the spirit of God was in Joseph, but the first time the text says God filled someone, it's none of those.
It's a man named Bezalel. And the spirit fills him not to preach or work miracles, but to work gold and silver and bronze, cut stones, carve wood, and make beautiful things.
The tabernacle, the tent where God would dwell among the people, needs building. And God picks the person who's good with his hands.

teach.b: Moses tells the people, in the King James Bible, that God has called Bezalel by name, "And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship."
Wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and then, without a pause, workmanship. Skill with your hands sits in the same breath as wisdom. In this book, making something well is a spiritual gift.

teach.h: PUT IN HIS HEART TO TEACH.
teach.b: He's given a partner, Oholiab, from another tribe, and God put it in their hearts to teach. So the gift isn't hoarded.
It's passed on, workshop style, to everyone the text calls wise-hearted: women spinning blue and purple yarn, men carving acacia wood, jewelers setting stones.
Whole sections of Exodus go to curtains and clasps, lampstands and loops, measured down to the cubit. People skip those chapters. The Bible takes its time there, as if to say: this matters too.
His name is lovely as well: Bezalel means in the shadow of God. And notice the timing. This comes right after the golden calf.

teach.h: GOLD FOR A CALF, GOLD FOR A TENT.
teach.b: The people's gold went into an idol; now gold, given freely, goes into a place for God to dwell. Same material, same hands, two directions.
Christians have taken this passage as a blessing on every kind of craft: the stonemasons of the great cathedrals, quilters and carpenters, the person who fixes your car well.

teach.h: FILLED WITH THE SPIRIT OF GOD.
teach.b: In this story, the spirit of God fills a workshop before it fills a pulpit.

how: Many Christians see craft and good work as a way of honoring God, and churches have long blessed builders, artists and artisans; some congregations hold services blessing tools or the work of people's hands.

o: a prophet's hands that worked great miracles
a priest's hands raised to bless the people
a craftsman's skill, filled with the spirit of God

games.q: who's who at the tabernacle — tap the pairs.
p: filled with the spirit for craft
his partner, also given to teach

s: the first person said to be filled with the spirit of God is a prophet
it's Bezalel, a craftsman, filled for workmanship as well as wisdom.
Bezalel was given the gift of teaching others
God put it in his heart to teach, him and Oholiab.
the building of the tabernacle comes right after the golden calf
the plans come first, in chapters 25 to 31; the building follows the calf, from chapter 35: gold for an idol, then gold given freely.

games.q: God's dwelling place has to be built in the desert. who does God choose to lead the work?
games.why: Bezalel, filled with the spirit of God in wisdom and in all manner of workmanship. the gift is skill with his hands.

practice: Make something small with care: fold a cloth perfectly, wash one cup slowly all the way around, or set three things on a table so they look right together.
Pay attention to the material in your hands, its weight and its texture, as if the work itself were an offering. If you pray, you can offer it.

wordCard.voice: Bezalel's hands. The craftsman of the tabernacle, the first person the Bible says was filled with the spirit of God, for wisdom and for workmanship.

orig.note: Hebrew: Bezalel, usually read as 'in the shadow of God'.

carryVoice: Your line: craft is spiritual. Even curtains and clasps can be holy work. Four hundred days, and counting.

sources.q: And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship
